        Disclaimer

        Coffees come from roasters’ own shop listings, checked every day. Not affiliated with any roaster. Roasters can ask to be removed at any time. Your journal, bags, equipment, scan photos and settings stay on this device. Only how a brew of a listed coffee tasted is counted, anonymously, to make the recipes better.

        Methods
        • V60James Hoffmann’s Better 1-Cup and Ultimate V60, Tetsu Kasuya’s 4:6 and 10-Pour, Scott Rao’s bloom & spin, Onyx Coffee Lab’s V60, CAFEC’s Osmotic Flow (ratio, temperature and technique; the pour weights and times are ours), Matt Winton’s Five-Pour, Lance Hedrick’s double bloom.
        • V60 NEOEvery V60 method, 2 clicks finer and about 15 s shorter, because the same recipe drained 34 s faster in the NEO in Gizmodo Japan’s side-by-side. Pours centre-out, bed kept covered, as Barista Magazine’s test drive advises. Hario publishes no NEO recipe, so this is our estimate. Tetsu Kasuya’s 10-Pour is written for the NEO and keeps its own grind.
        • Kalita WaveGeorge Howell’s 155 guide.
        • April BrewerApril Coffee’s base recipe.
        • OreaMartin Woelfl’s 2024 World Brewers Cup recipe.
        • MelittaThe technique is from Revelator Coffee’s Melitta guide (bloom, circles off the paper, pause and carry on); the weights, ratio and temperature are ours.
        • OrigamiCarlos Medina’s 2023 World Brewers Cup recipe.
        • ChemexBlue Bottle’s brew guide, its five pours scaled to the dose.
        • Hario SwitchTetsu Kasuya’s Hybrid Method.
        • Clever DripperJames Hoffmann’s Ultimate Clever technique.
        • AeroPressJames Hoffmann’s Ultimate AeroPress technique, standard way up; the inverted version is our adaptation of it. Tim Wendelboe’s café recipe.
        • French PressJames Hoffmann’s Ultimate French Press technique.
        • EspressoThe modern 1:2 in about 25–30 s, after James Hoffmann’s Understanding Espresso series; longer for lighter roasts, shorter for a ristretto.
        • Bialetti Moka ExpressJames Hoffmann’s Ultimate Moka Pot technique.
        • CuppingThe SCA cupping protocol (8.25 g to 150 ml, 93°C, break at 3 to 5 minutes; we use 4).
        • MoccamasterMoccamaster’s own guide gives 55 g a litre; we use 60 g, the strong end of the SCA’s 55 g a litre, give or take 10%.
        • Cold brewThe ratio and dilution are from Ceremony Coffee’s guide; the 12 to 18 hour fridge steep is ours, in line with Liang et al. 2024.
        • GrindComandante C40 clicks, counted from zero. Other grinders converted from those clicks with Honest Coffee Guide’s grind charts.
